key_insight: LLM judges can reliably screen patient-facing content for safety and factual accuracy, but they are less aligned with human experts on communication quality.
clinical_relevance: These automated judges could help scale oversight of AI-generated patient communication, especially for high-stakes settings like informed consent, while still requiring patient-centered calibration.
method: Built a stakeholder-informed 7-criterion rubric covering safety, reliability, and communication quality.
Validated the rubric on ICON-Bench using clinician reference ratings.
Benchmarked 19 LLM judges across multiple implementation strategies against clinician and patient-advocate assessments.
evidence_signal: Clinician ratings showed strong interrater reliability, and LLM judges matched clinicians well for safety screening and factual verification (Spearman rho > 0.80) but less well for communication quality (rho < 0.60).
watch_item: General-purpose models outperformed safety-specialized guard models in this setting, and patient advocates rated communication quality more strictly than clinicians or LLM judges, highlighting the need for recalibration.
paper_title: Validating LLM judges for automated oversight of patient communication
